turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - alloy_pair_target_train.csv: 300 samples described by composition in wt% — C, Mn, Si, Cr, Ni, Mo, V, Nb, Co, Al, Ti, Cu
      (Fe is the balance: Fe = 100 − Σ of the others) — plus processing parameters
      (solutionizing_temp, aging_temp, aging_time, cooling_rate) and categorical
      settings heat_treatment (annealed | quenched | quench_temper | solution_aged)
      and route (cast | wrought | AM), with the measured 0.2 % proof yield strength in MPa (the `target` column).
  - alloy_pair_target_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE recipes whose yield strength was NOT measured, with the same columns plus `candidate_id` and no `target`.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have a yield strength CLOSEST to 1051 MPa — not the highest, the closest to that value — then select the 5 best candidates from the pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
# Analysis

Since 1051 MPa exceeds even the highest observed training target (908.5 MPa), the closest achievable predictions come from candidates whose full feature vectors (composition **and** processing/categorical variables) most closely match the training rows with the **highest** measured yield strengths.

**Approach:**
1. Identified the highest-yield training rows (908.5, 899.2, 863.9, 771.9, 737.7, 734.1, 726.4, 721.6, 709.2 MPa …) and examined their full profiles (composition + heat_treatment + route + thermal parameters).
2. For each pool candidate, searched for the training row with minimum multi-feature distance (C, Cr, Ni, Mo, V, Nb, Co, Al, Ti, Cu), respecting matching heat_treatment/route since these strongly gate the achievable strength ceiling (quench_temper > solution_aged > quenched > annealed in the training data; extreme corner compositions, e.g. Mo=6+Co=15+Cr=22 combos, consistently gave very low strengths).
3. Verified each candidate match wasn't coincidentally closer to a *lower*-target row (cross-checked against several alternative neighbors).

**Key matches found (candidate → nearest high-strength training analog, approx. distance):**

| Candidate | Matched training target | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| c079 | 908.5 MPa | Near-perfect match: C, Cr, Mo, Co, Al, Cu, V, sol/aging temps, aging time, cooling rate all align closely (quench_temper/AM) |
| c017 | 863.9 MPa | Excellent match on C, Ni, Mo, V, Nb, Co, sol_temp, aging_time (quench_temper/wrought) |
| c008 | 737.7 MPa | Extremely tight match (distance <1) across nearly all features (quench_temper/cast) |
| c085 | 726.4 MPa | Good match on Cr, Ni, aging profile (quench_temper/wrought) |
| c039 | 721.6 MPa | Good match on C, Ni, Mo, aging_time, cooling_rate (quench_temper/wrought) |

These five candidates are predicted to have the highest yield strengths in the pool (~700–910 MPa range), making them the closest available approximations to the target of 1051 MPa — no pool candidate is expected to approach 1051 exactly, but these represent the top end of the achievable strength distribution based on training analogs.

Final: c079, c017, c008, c085, c039
